To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mTOR kinase inhibitor (AZD8055) can synergistically enhance the antitumor effects of an agonist anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody (αCD40) in a model of liver metastatic renal cell cancer, through a mechanism that involves activation of the innate immune system and the production of IFN-γ.
the combination of an mTOR kinase inhibitor and an agonistic CD40 antibody elicits synergistic antitumoral responses in a model for renal cell carcinoma metastasis.

the ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor AZD 8055 enhances the antitumor activity of an agonistic CD40 antibody in a murine model of metastatic RCC by increasing CD8(+) effector T cells, NK cells, and macrophages and inducing the secretion of IFN-γ.

the development of a combination immunotherapy for the treatment of cancer.
the use of mTOR inhibitors in combination with immunotherapy.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches to cancer treatment.
